acquisition_method: A data dependent mass spectrometric method was employed
alkylation_concentration: after reduction (5′mM DTT, 30′min) and alkylation (10′mM iodoacetamide, 20′min, in the dark)
alkylation_reagent: after reduction (5′mM DTT, 30′min) and alkylation (10′mM iodoacetamide, 20′min, in the dark)
cleavage_agent: proteins were digested for 3′h by Lys-C (Wako) at a protein:enzyme ratio of 100:1. Samples were diluted with 10′mM ammonium bicarbonate to 2′M urea prior to overnight trypsin digestion (Sequencing grade, Promega) at a protein:enzyme ratio of 100:1.
collision_energy: fragmented using higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) (normalized collision energy 25)
fractionation_method: Peptides (180′μg) were separated by in-solution isoelectric focusing (OFFGEL fractionator, Agilent) into 12 fractions over a pH range of 3–10.
fragmentation_method: fragmented using higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) (normalized collision energy 25)
mass_analyzer: inferred: EASY nLC-II coupled to a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany)

instrument.evidence: EASY nLC-II coupled to a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany)

ptm.value: N-terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation, cysteine carbamidomethylation
ptm.evidence: allowing for maximum two missed cleavages, N-terminal acetylation and methionine oxidation as variable modifications and cysteine carbamidomethylation as fixed modification
